headline: GOLD FALLS $210 TO $4,390 AS JACKSON HOLE DATA GAUNTLET OPENS — THREE MACRO PRINTS BEFORE WARSH SPEAKS THURSDAY
snippet: Gold opened Monday August 24 at $4,390 per ounce — a $210 pullback from last week's $4,600+ high — and silver retreated to $64.74 from its all-time high above $70, as markets shed risk ahead of the most consequential data week of August: ADP employment, preliminary Q2 GDP, Core PCE, and the University of Michigan inflation survey all print before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole address on August 28. GoldSilver.com frames the pullback as a harvesting of last week's gains rather than a trend reversal, noting that gold is still up approximately 10% in August from near $4,000 — its best single-month gain of 2026. For TSX-V and ASX gold and silver junior investors, the magnitude of the weekly range ($200-300 per ounce in gold alone) illustrates just how macro-sensitive the entire mining equity complex has become in this environment. The $4,450-$4,500 zone is cited as a potential re-entry level if any of the three data prints delivers a hawkish surprise before Thursday.

headline: COT REPORT AUG 21: GOLD SPECULATORS HOLD 252,603 LONGS BUT ARE NOWHERE NEAR HISTORIC EXTREMES — STRUCTURAL BUYERS ARE DRIVING THIS RUN
snippet: The August 21, 2026 CFTC Commitments of Traders report — covering positions as of Tuesday August 18 — showed managed money holding 252,603 long and 33,108 short COMEX gold contracts, with total open interest at 561,817 contracts. Despite gold's 10% August surge, the net speculative long position remains well below the historic extremes that have historically preceded major market tops. Silver's managed money net long also sits below all-time record levels, consistent with the thesis that this rally is being driven by real-money central bank buying and physical demand rather than speculative froth. GoldSeek's COT analysis notes that this positioning configuration — a metals bull market with muted speculative participation — is historically one of the most constructive setups available: when the momentum-chasing funds who missed the first leg eventually pile in on a pullback, they compress the remaining discount rapidly. For retail investors tracking whether gold and silver are entering a blow-off top, the COT data argues the opposite: the speculative wave that amplifies moves in either direction has not yet materialized.

headline: AUG 22 PRECIOUS METALS WRAP: GOLD AND SILVER HOLD NEAR HIGHS AS MEXICO AND PERU MINERS EXTEND WEEKLY GAINS
snippet: Gold and silver extended their weekly gains into Saturday August 22 trading, with The Rio Times tracking how the metals' bull run translated into equity gains for Mexican and Peruvian primary silver and gold producers — the two countries that together account for roughly 40% of global silver mine supply. Mexican names including First Majestic Silver and Fresnillo, and Peruvian producers including Buenaventura, outperformed spot metal as high operating leverage to elevated silver prices amplified investor returns. Silver had held near its all-time high above $70 per ounce set earlier in the week. The Aug 22 wrap provided context on what the sustained rally means for regional Latin American mining equities, where many producers carry AISC well below current realized prices, generating margin expansion that has not yet been fully re-rated by the market. This regional equity follow-through — when mining equities in key producing nations begin to outperform the metal itself — is historically a mid-cycle signal rather than a blow-off indicator.

headline: K2 GOLD DRILLS 39.62m AT 5.35 g/t IN CALIFORNIA MOJAVE — FIRST RESULTS FROM LARGEST-EVER PROGRAM CONFIRM HIGH-GRADE OXIDE DISTRICT
snippet: K2 Gold (TSX-V: KTO) released the first three assay results from its 14,000-metre 2026 drill campaign at the Mojave Project in California's San Bernardino County, confirming a high-grade oxide gold system at the Dragonfly target: hole DF26-020 returned 39.62 metres grading 5.35 g/t gold from 51.82 metres downhole, including a 25.91-metre interval at 7.14 g/t; DF26-019 cut 10.67 metres at 7.75 g/t; and DF26-018 returned 18.29 metres at 3.77 g/t including 7.62 metres at 7.48 g/t. Mineralization is confirmed over approximately 400 metres of strike within the 6.5-kilometre Eastside Gold Trend and remains open along strike and at depth, with 12 additional assays pending from holes TR26-40 through TR26-50. This is the largest drill program ever undertaken at Mojave — 15 holes totalling 2,630 metres completed so far — with drilling continuing through at least September 2026. KTO gained approximately 6% to C$0.89 on the day of announcement. For investors tracking discovery-stage leverage, oxide gold systems in fully permitted California ground carry a path-to-production premium: the heap-leach processing model for low-sulphidation oxide systems is faster and lower-capex than equivalent underground or sulphide discoveries.

headline: SILVERCORP METALS DRILLS 212.5m AT 1.68 g/t GOLD IN KYRGYZSTAN — FIRST BATCH OF 60,000m CAMPAIGN OPENS TWO NEW STRUCTURES
snippet: Silvercorp Metals (TSX: SVM, NYSE American: SVM) reported the first batch of results from a 50,000–60,000 metre in-fill and step-out drill program at the Kyzyltash project in Kyrgyzstan via its 70%-owned ZAAV subsidiary, with hole DH26M687 returning 212.5 metres grading 1.68 g/t gold — a remarkable bulk-tonnage interval that included sub-zones of 3.26 g/t over 29.5 metres and 3.05 g/t over 25.5 metres. Hole DH26M818 cut 47 metres at 3.95 g/t gold including 13.65 g/t over 4.5 metres, while DH26M686 intersected six mineralized structures including 39 metres at 4.79 g/t gold with a 6-metre interval at 22.23 g/t. The 29-hole dataset covering 3,640 metres of Main Zone strike confirmed multiple broad zones open at depth and along strike, and identified two newly recognized sub-parallel structures not previously modelled. The fully permitted project's 60,000-metre program is designed to convert inferred resources to the measured-and-indicated category, with an updated resource estimate planned as an input to an upcoming economic study. Kyzyltash's broad interval grades are particularly notable against a gold price above $4,400 per ounce: a 200-metre gold intercept at 1.68 g/t — even at moderate cutoffs — supports the geometry of a multi-million-ounce deposit.

headline: CAMECO MCARTHUR RIVER SUPPLY ROUTE SEVERED BY SPRING FLOODING — ATHABASCA BASIN SURFACE INFRASTRUCTURE RISK EXPOSED IN MID-YEAR REPORT
snippet: Cameco's mid-year operational update disclosed that spring flooding caused the collapse of a bridge on the primary surface supply route to its McArthur River uranium mine and Key Lake mill in northern Saskatchewan — temporarily suspending Key Lake production and constraining McArthur River mining rates for approximately two weeks in May 2026 before operations resumed. Cameco confirmed it remains on track for full-year guidance despite the disruption. The incident is a structural reminder for Athabasca Basin investors: Canada's most productive uranium district depends on a fragile surface access network that cannot be quickly rerouted through the wetland terrain of the Athabasca lowlands. For junior uranium developers in the basin, this logistics reality elevates the strategic value of any existing permitted road or surface infrastructure within range of NexGen's Rook I and Denison's Wheeler River projects — assets that take years to permit and cannot be replicated on short notice. The McArthur River disruption is historically rare but not unprecedented; it joins permafrost degradation as an underappreciated physical risk in sell-side Athabasca Basin project valuations.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT TRUCE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — 90 DAYS UNTIL $6.5 TRILLION IN GLOBAL ECONOMIC ACTIVITY FACES SUPPLY RISK
snippet: The 12-month suspension of China's expanded rare earth export controls — agreed as part of the Xi-Trump trade framework following the October 2025 announcements — is set to expire on November 10, 2026, with no extension yet confirmed and limited progress made in reducing the global supply chain's dependence on Chinese rare earth processing. Mining Technology's analysis notes that the April 2025 export licensing regime was never part of the truce and continues to restrict volumes, while the October 2025 controls — covering a broader set of products and processing steps — are what lapses in 90 days. If the truce expires without renewal or a negotiated extension, the IEA estimates $6.5 trillion in annual global economic activity faces direct supply exposure, spanning aerospace, defence, semiconductor fabrication, AI data centre infrastructure, and clean energy equipment. Processing remains the structural bottleneck: while Australia, Canada, and the United States all mine rare earth minerals, the majority continues to flow to Chinese refineries before entering downstream supply chains. For TSX-V and ASX rare earth investors, November 10 is a hard policy catalyst: projects with credible non-Chinese processing paths — including those supplying Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill and Lynas's Malaysian facility — are in a fundamentally different position than projects without offtake destinations.

headline: RETAIL POURS $419M INTO GDX IN AUGUST — GOLD MINERS SURGING 23.75% THIS MONTH AS VALUATION MULTIPLES HIT 41-QUARTER LOWS
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) is on pace to record $419 million in August retail inflows — its strongest monthly intake since February — as the ETF's 23.75% August gain brings GDX back from a 38.9% mid-year correction and toward its March 2026 all-time high. Benzinga highlights six gold mining ETFs — including GDX, GDXJ, SIL, SILJ, GOEX, and SGDM — that are capturing the August rotation into mining equities. The fundamental picture underlying the inflows is exceptional: the GDX top-25 components are trading at their lowest trailing-twelve-month P/E ratios in at least 41 quarters, with elite majors priced at just 16.5x earnings despite all-in sustaining costs that have risen far more slowly than gold prices. The free cash flow-to-EV yield of the sector is at record highs. For retail investors tracking capital flows, the $419 million inflow figure matters not just as a sentiment signal but as a supply-demand dynamic: passive ETF inflows must be deployed into a relatively illiquid universe of mining stocks, creating mechanical buying pressure that is independent of individual analyst upgrades or earnings surprises.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD MINERS' Q2'26 FUNDAMENTALS SHOW RECORD FREE CASH FLOWS — AND THE MARKET STILL HASN'T FULLY PRICED THEM IN
snippet: GoldSeek's quarterly deep-dive into gold miner fundamentals for Q2 2026 — covering the earnings reports from Newmont, Barrick, and Agnico Eagle — finds that despite record operating margins, the sector's equity valuations do not yet fully reflect the sustained price environment. Newmont posted adjusted EBITDA of $3.8 billion and record Q2 free cash flow of $2.2 billion with AISC of approximately $910 per ounce, while Agnico Eagle Mines achieved record Q2 free cash flow of $1.33 billion with AISC near $880 per ounce. Barrick reported $1.22 billion in Q2 net earnings on revenues up 44% year-over-year with AISC around $1,866 per ounce for gold. G Mining also reiterated production targets but raised annual cost guidance by 7%, reflecting labour and currency pressures in Brazil — a reminder that not all producers are equal beneficiaries of higher prices. The GoldSeek analysis — from a preferred source for gold mining opinion — frames the key disconnect: at $4,400+ gold, these cash generation rates imply balance sheets that could fund 3–5 years of exploration and development from a single year's free cash flow, yet most senior producers still trade at significant discounts to the NPV implied by current spot prices.

headline: LITHIUM PRICES AT TWO-YEAR HIGHS AFTER 84% RECOVERY FROM 2024 LOWS — WHAT'S DRIVING THE SURGE AND WHICH JUNIORS BENEFIT
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices have recovered approximately 84% from their 2024 lows, reaching two-year highs in 2026, driven by a combination of accelerating EV adoption, surging energy storage buildout in China and the United States, constrained hard rock supply after mass project suspensions in 2023–2024, and EV battery supply chains rebuilding depleted inventories. The recovery has been uneven: battery-grade Chinese lithium carbonate recovered sharply earlier in 2026 before some volatility, while spodumene concentrate from Australia held at $915–920 per tonne — well above the marginal cost of production for most tier-one hard rock operations. Multiple Australian mines that were suspended in 2023–2024 have since restarted, including Mineral Resources' Bald Hill and Core Lithium's Finniss, but analysts caution that the pace of restarts matters: too much new supply too fast risks repeating the 2022–2024 cycle. For TSX-V and ASX lithium junior investors, the INN analysis frames the structural question that matters most: whether the 2026 price recovery is demand-driven and durable (as in 2020–2022), or inventory-driven and temporary (as the early 2023 recovery proved to be before collapsing). Current EV adoption data and the energy storage build rate in China lean toward the former.
